evidence: H1 2026 consolidated revenue grew 18.0% YoY and order backlog rose 25.2% from 2025 year-end to KRW 9.5535T.
The company has built a differentiated submarine/HVDC stack spanning 525kV cable manufacturing, installation capability through LS Marine Solution, and new U.S. capacity through LS GreenLink.
counter_evidence: Offshore-wind project cancellations show that backlog and reservations can be exposed to project financing, permitting and customer cancellation risk.

evidence: Large multi-year TenneT, MOG2 and U.S. 345kV projects demonstrate customer willingness to award long-duration, high-voltage cable and installation scopes.
The business is moving from cable supply toward turnkey design/supply/installation/test, which can increase content per project and customer integration.
counter_evidence: The supplied filings do not independently quantify switching costs, bid win rates, customer concentration or cancellation penalties across the backlog.

evidence: 525kV HVDC mass production, Donghae submarine capacity expansion and cable-laying capability increase technical qualification and execution barriers.
H1 2026 high/extra-high-voltage cable utilization was 99.4%, consistent with tight demand for core high-value capacity.
counter_evidence: Global competitors including Prysmian, Nexans and Chinese cable makers are expanding, while project awards remain bid-based and exposed to capacity additions.

evidence: FY2025 OCF was KRW 729.1B against KRW 489.5B of PPE purchases, while H1 2026 operating margin improved to about 5.27% from 4.32%.
Backlog growth and near-full utilization support the economic rationale for capacity investment.
counter_evidence: H1 2026 OCF was negative KRW 704.2B and OCF less PPE purchases was negative KRW 950.2B as inventory, receivables and other working-capital requirements expanded sharply.
2026 investment plan totals KRW 1.2881T, with KRW 808.4B still expected after H1; returns on U.S., Mexico and submarine capacity are not yet observable.

evidence: Capital is being concentrated on submarine/HVDC, installation, U.S. and Mexico capacity that is directionally aligned with backlog and electrification demand.
The company maintains A1 commercial-paper and A+ (Positive) bond ratings and was compliant with disclosed debt covenants.
counter_evidence: A 7.85% rights offering in 2025, KRW 0.2T exchangeable bonds, rising borrowings and continuing equity/investment commitments indicate aggressive funding needs.
Two disclosed wind-project cancellations demonstrate that committed capacity can outlive individual project economics.

evidence: At June 2026 cash plus financial-institution deposits was about KRW 1.219T, credit ratings were A1 and A+ (Positive), and covenant compliance was reported.
The company retains access to commercial paper, bonds and bank funding.
counter_evidence: Consolidated borrowings and bonds increased to KRW 4.016T from KRW 2.935T at 2025 year-end, while H1 OCF was deeply negative and liabilities reached KRW 8.271T.

evidence: The operating evidence is materially stronger than a generic cable-cycle thesis.
counter_evidence: No synchronized K-OTC quote, control/minority discount framework, fully diluted share bridge or reverse DCF was completed.
missing_data: Reliable synchronized K-OTC transaction price/liquidity, minority-shareholder discount, net debt bridge, 10-year owner-cash scenarios and reverse expectations.

evidence: A sustained global HVDC/submarine-grid buildout could create multi-year compounding if LS Cable's manufacturing-plus-installation position scales.
counter_evidence: K-OTC illiquidity, 92.63% parent ownership, leverage and project-cancellation risk make per-share asymmetry price-dependent and governance-dependent.
missing_data: Synchronized valuation, project-level margin/ROIC, backlog conversion, minority liquidity and exit-path analysis.

evidence: FY2025 financial statements and internal control received unqualified/appropriate audit opinions; H1 2026 review found no material unfair presentation under K-IFRS 1034.
items.resolution_needed: Continue routine audit, project-accounting and related-party monitoring.

evidence: H1 2026 OCF was -KRW 704.2B while financing cash flow was +KRW 908.0B and total borrowings/bonds rose by about KRW 1.081T from year-end.
items.resolution_needed: Build a multi-year funding model covering working capital, capex, U.S./Mexico investments, maturities and project cancellation stress without assuming repeated equity issuance.

evidence: The company issued 1,752,718 new common shares in the 2025 rights offering, disclosed as 7.85% of the relevant existing share base.
items.resolution_needed: Determine whether the rights issue was exceptional or the start of repeated equity funding, and reconcile treasury shares, exchangeable bonds and future capital needs.

evidence: Revenue and operating profit rose strongly, but H1 cash conversion deteriorated because inventory increased by KRW 645.3B and receivables by KRW 255.0B in the operating cash-flow bridge.
items.resolution_needed: Track backlog-to-revenue-to-cash conversion, customer advances, inventory turns and cancellation/rework costs over at least four quarters.

evidence: 2026 planned investment is KRW 1.2881T, including significant new U.S./Mexico/submarine capacity, while realized post-tax returns are not yet visible.
items.resolution_needed: Estimate post-tax cash ROIC by major new plant/project and compare with the Korea hurdle rate used by the harness.

evidence: Technology/capacity evidence is strong, but the industry remains competitive and project awards can be cancelled or rebid.
items.resolution_needed: Independent evidence on qualification cycles, lead times, win/loss rates, cancellation protections, pricing retention and competitor capacity.

evidence: No synchronized K-OTC price and reverse valuation were performed.
items.resolution_needed: Use an executable/representative K-OTC price with liquidity discount and minority-control considerations, then reverse DCF normalized owner cash.

evidence: ㈜LS owns 92.63% of common shares; copper represents about 65% of production raw-material cost; project/customer concentration is not fully quantified in the supplied reports.
items.resolution_needed: Quantify top-project/customer exposure, raw-material pass-through economics and minority-holder governance protections.

evidence: High leverage, negative interim cash conversion, K-OTC illiquidity and controlling-shareholder concentration can impair minority per-share value even if backlog grows.
items.resolution_needed: Complete a price-linked bear/base/bull model with debt reduction, dilution, cancellation, working-capital normalization and minority-liquidity scenarios.

core_thesis: LS전선은 단순 전선 제조업체보다 HVDC·해저케이블 제조와 시공을 결합한 전력망 인프라 플랫폼으로 이동하고 있으며, 수주잔고와 고부가 생산설비 가동률은 구조적 수요를 지지한다. 그러나 2026년 상반기에는 재고·매출채권 중심의 운전자본 팽창으로 현금흐름이 크게 악화되고 차입금과 투자계획이 동시에 늘었다. 따라서 투자 핵심은 수주 증가가 실제 높은 세후 현금 ROIC와 주당 가치로 전환되는지를 검증하는 것이다.
strongest_bear_thesis: 전력망/HVDC 슈퍼사이클이 실제이더라도 프로젝트 취소, 구리 가격과 운전자본 부담, 미국·멕시코·해저 설비 증설의 낮은 ROIC, 반복적인 외부자금 조달, 92.63% 지배주주 구조와 K-OTC 비유동성이 결합되면 소액주주의 현금복리 수익은 기대보다 훨씬 낮을 수 있다.
falsifiers: 수주잔고가 늘어도 4개 분기 이상 영업현금흐름과 재고회전이 정상화되지 않는다.
신규 해저/HVDC 설비와 해외 공장이 한국 주식용 hurdle을 넘는 세후 현금 ROIC를 만들지 못한다.
대형 프로젝트 취소/지연이 반복되며 수주잔고의 현금전환율이 구조적으로 낮아진다.
차입 증가 또는 반복 유상증자로 주당 owner cash 증가율이 절대 이익 증가율을 지속적으로 하회한다.
next_evidence: 수주잔고 계약별 취소권, 선수금, 마일스톤, 이익률 및 현금회수 구조.
미국 GreenLink, 멕시코 부스덕트/고전압전선, 동해 해저케이블 증설의 투자액·가동률·매출·마진·운전자본을 연결한 프로젝트별 cash ROIC.
최근 4~8분기 재고·매출채권·계약자산·계약부채 브리지와 OCF 정상화 경로.
K-OTC 거래가격·유동성·지배주주 할인/프리미엄을 반영한 reverse DCF 및 Bear/Base/Bull.
